A2 ön-kayıtta hash'lenerek dondurulur. | v2: chain-3 istatistik gücü için +6 soru (ORTA-9/A2 donma koşulu; toplam 56, chain-3 n=10). | v3 (KRİTİK-7/F1): chain>=2 sorulara suggested_args_per_step ($prev.X policy türetmesi) + args_pinned; tam-zincir referans-graf için. | CROSS-LINGUAL: her soruya question_en eklendi (prereg-v2.0).
balance_report:
Final set: exactly 50 questions, 12-13 per stakeholder (residential 12, commercial 13, distribution 13, state 12), satisfying the 12-13 band and the '>=1 cross scale_focus per stakeholder' requirement (res-11/res-12 cross; com-10 cross; dis-09/dis-10 cross; sta-07/sta-10 cross).

Two edits from the raw candidate pool:
1. Dropped 1 residential item (Bursa 5kW NPV+MC) as a near-duplicate of an already-accepted feasibility+MC chain (res-08), bringing residential from 13 candidates down to the target 12.
2. Rejected 1 state item ('highest IRR' policy-mechanism question) because run_policy_scenario's declared outputs (npv/payback/government cost) do not include IRR — the tool literally cannot answer it, making it an unanswerable/hallucination-bait item rather than a legitimate benchmark question.
3. Corrected one chain_length in-place (not rejected): com-13 (Antalya hotel 70kW+50kWh, net-metering vs FiT NPV comparison) was labeled chain_length=3 in the candidate set but actually requires only 2 tool calls — run_policy_scenario returns all 9 mechanisms (including both net metering and FiT) in a single call, so 'comparing two of the nine' is not a second policy call. Relabeled feasibility(1)+policy(1)=2.

Chain-length distribution achieved: chain1=27, chain2=19, chain3=4 (sum=50). This falls short of the requested ~32/~12/~6 split — there are simply too many chain-2-shaped questions and too few chain-1/chain-3-shaped questions in the original 50-candidate pool once schema-invalid and duplicate items are removed (residential and commercial supplied only 6/1 and 6/0 usable chain1/chain3 items respectively, all of which were already used). Reaching 32/12/6 exactly would have required either inventing new questions (outside this editorial task's scope — only dedup/reject was authorized) or arbitrarily discarding valid, non-duplicate, schema-correct questions purely to hit a ratio, which would have reduced coverage quality. Recommend that future candidate-question drafting for this benchmark bias toward more single-call (chain1) 'quick fact' questions and more genuine 3-tool chained questions (chain3), and fewer 2-tool 'compute A, then compute B for comparison' questions, to hit the target distribution without needing to cut usable content.

Other schema notes applied during editing: all cities normalized to lowercase from the allowed set (ankara/istanbul/izmir/antalya/konya/bursa); all panel_kw (4-70) and bess_kwh (0-50) values fall within the tool's 0.5-100 / 0-100 ranges, no violations found; EV-mention questions (res-05) were kept because the tool has no EV parameter but the question's actual numeric ask (system cost, savings) is still fully answerable by simulate_pv_bess treating EV context as narrative color, not a required argument.

rejected.question_tr: Bursa'da evim için 5 kW GES kurulumunun net bugünkü değerini hesapla ve sonucun ne kadar güvenilir olduğunu Monte Carlo simülasyonuyla teyit et.
rejected.reason: DEDUP: residential 'feasibility + Monte Carlo confirmation' pattern is already covered by the accepted res-08 (İzmir 6kW+10kWh feasibility+MC, chain2). Near-identical structure/intent (single feasibility call followed by MC on the same system) with no new tool combination or numeric focus; dropped to keep residential at the 12-13 target band without redundant coverage.

rejected.question_tr: En yüksek IRR'yi sağlayan teşvik mekanizması hangisi, 600.000 TL yatırım ve yıllık 85.000 TL tasarruf senaryosunda?
